question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Nvidia)

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 to $108B +/-2% (Aug 26, 2026). Over the last eight quarters it beat its guidance midpoint by 2.5-7.9% (median ~5%; Q2 FY27 was $96.2B vs a $91B guide). Applied to $108B, that gives a median near $113.3B and a 10-90 range of about $110.5-116.5B. Supply limits through FY28 cap upside, while the Vera Rubin ramp (~$20B) and excess demand support a strong beat; there has been no miss on the midpoint, so a print below $105B is very unlikely. Market check: Manifold 'Terminator2' market (4 traders, 18 trades, too thin to anchor) shows <110: 8%, 110-112: 40%, 112-114: 26%, 114-116: 17%, >=116: 10%; no Polymarket or Kalshi contract found. About 12% sits above $116B (open upper bound); the percentiles are conditional on landing in range.
calls.dossier:
- Nvidia guided Q3 FY2027 (quarter ending late Oct 2026) revenue to $108.0B +/-2% ($105.8-110.2B), gross margin ~74%; guide assumes zero China data-center compute revenue (Aug 26, 2026 release; webull/fool/kucoin summaries).
- Vera Rubin production shipments began August 2026; mgmt expects ~20% of Q3 data-center revenue (~$20B) (Yahoo/Tom's Hardware, Aug-Sep 2026).
- CFO Kress: supply expected to stay a bottleneck at least through end of FY2028 (Q2 call transcript, Aug 26, 2026).
- Q2 FY27 actual $96.22B vs company guide ~$91B (+5.7%) and LSEG consensus $92.17B; data center $89.0B (Aug 26, 2026).
- Prior actual-vs-guide-midpoint history (computed from releases): Q3 FY25 35.08 vs 32.5 (+7.9%); Q4 FY25 39.33 vs 37.5 (+4.9%); Q1 FY26 44.06 vs 43.0 (+2.5%, H20 export hit); Q2 FY26 46.74 vs 45.0 (+3.9%); Q3 FY26 57.01 vs 54.0 (+5.6%); Q4 FY26 68.13 vs 65.0 (+4.8%); Q1 FY27 81.62 vs ~78 (+~4.6%); Q2 FY27 96.22 vs 91 (+5.7%). Range 2.5-7.9% over these 8 quarters; no miss of the midpoint.
- Sell-side consensus for Q3 FY27 revenue: ~$108.8-108.9B (MarketBeat/others), one source ~$111.4B; EPS consensus $2.49, whisper $2.60 (EarningsWhispers, Nov 2026).
- Report date: Nov 17, 2026 per EarningsWhispers (MarketBeat lists Nov 18); before the question's Nov 25 date, and the first report after Sep 30, 2026.
- Status quo: Nvidia prints above the top of its guide range, as in each of the last 8 quarters.
- Resolves off the headline total revenue in Nvidia's Q3 FY27 8-K/press release, not the data-center segment and not later revisions.
- Event window: first earnings release after 2026-09-30 -> expected ~Nov 17-18, 2026; as of Nov 1 the fiscal quarter has ended (late Oct) but nothing has been reported.
- Downside candidates: supply/yield problems on the Rubin ramp, new export rules, customer timing shifts. Upside candidates: faster Rubin ramp, any China H20/B-series sales not in the guide.
- Searched but not found: any mid-quarter pre-announcement or guidance revision for Q3 FY27; Kalshi or Polymarket contracts on this revenue figure.
calls.reference_class: Nvidia quarterly revenue vs its own prior-quarter guidance midpoint, Q3 FY25 to Q2 FY27 (8 quarters)

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $108B ±2% (range 105.84-110.16B), excluding China DC compute. Over the last six quarters actual revenue beat the guide midpoint by 2.5-5.7% (Q2 FY27: 91B guide -> 96.2B actual, +5.7%), and FY25 beats were 5-8.5%. A ~4.5-5% beat implies ~$113B, matching whisper numbers of 113-114B; published sell-side consensus is ~$108.8B. Market check: Polymarket/Kalshi/bookmakers none found. Manifold has a thin market (4 holders, 18 trades) with buckets <110: 8%, 110-112: 40%, 112-114: 26%, 114-116: 17%, >=116: 10%. That is the same contract on GAAP total revenue but too illiquid to anchor on, so it is used as weak evidence that slightly lowers the median. Upper escape: a beat over 7.4% happened in FY25 and China sales would be extra. Lower escape: missing the guide floor, never seen recently. Earnings are confirmed for Nov 17, 2026, inside the window.

calls.reasoning: Guide $108B ±2% (excl. China). Over the last 8 quarters, revenue beat the guide midpoint by 2.5-7.9% (median ~5%), with no miss, which implies ~$113B. Sequential adds of ~$11-15B per quarter (+$14.6B would give ~$110.8B), CFO-stated supply limits and a thin Manifold market centred near $112B pull the median slightly lower. The Rubin ramp and growing absolute beats ($3.0B, $3.1B, $3.6B, $5.2B) support ~$113B. Upper escape (>7.4% beat) ~10%; lower escape needs a miss below the guide floor, ~1%.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on guidance ($108B ±2%), beat history (2.5-7.9% over midpoint) and report date (Nov 17-18, before Nov 25). Disputes: (1) whether a Manifold market exists: runs 1-2 report a thin 4-trader market, run 3 none; this could not be checked without web access, and I treat it as weak evidence only. (2) Consensus figures ($108.8B to $114B) vary by source and date and could not be settled; they were not load-bearing. (3) Upper-tail mass of 9-12% is a judgment call; I took 10% from 2 of 10 beats above 7.4%, both in FY25 with shrinking frequency since. I shaded the median to $112.8B because sequential-growth extrapolation (~$110.8B) and supply limits cut against the median-beat projection. I carried forward the beat-SD dispersion basis.
